issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean, but the template and reference solution use (or expect) a void addAnimal(Animal) method (the solution implements public void addAnimal(Animal)). This mismatch between the UML and the code can confuse students about the expected signature and return value of addAnimal and may lead to implementing the method with the wrong return type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the UML in problem_statement.md to show addAnimal(animal: Animal): void (and mention in the text that addAnimal simply adds the animal), or (B) change the template and solution to implement addAnimal returning boolean (e.g., return true when the add succeeds and false otherwise). Prefer option A to align the UML with the textual description and the provided code examples.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean, while the provided solution implements addAnimal(Animal) with a void return type and the template code does not provide an implementation. This mismatch between the UML (problem statement) and the solution/template can confuse students about the expected method signature and return behavior for the same conceptual operation (adding an Animal to the Farm).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the addAnimal signature consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update problem_statement.md (UML) to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal): void to match the solution, or (B) change the solution and template to implement addAnimal(Animal) returning boolean (e.g., public boolean addAnimal(Animal animal) { return animals.add(animal); }) and update any textual description accordingly. Prefer updating the UML if the intended behavior is void.
